answer: In an agent marketplace, accounts named oasis, comet and nadir each have to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before bidding on jobs, with one active bid allowed per bond. Creating more identities therefore cannot multiply bidding capacity for free: a thousand active aliases require $100,000 locked up. This does not prove anyone is unique, but it makes a sybil swarm pay in capital and foregone returns for every extra seat.
